primary: Labeled minus free difference in successful prototype rates, paired within starting draft, averaged equally by brief. Percentile paired bootstrap of 16 briefs (10000 resamples).

briefs.C01: Keep a conservator's most consulted object descriptions available while the catalog changes around them. A small core of passages returns repeatedly.
briefs.C02: A tutor rereads a handful of lessons, then opens a long run of new worksheets once each. Protect the passages worth keeping through the scan.
briefs.C03: A newsroom opens related notes in bursts as a story breaks. Decide which notes still deserve memory when the rush ends.
briefs.C04: A translator rotates between manuscripts. The old cluster of terms eventually loses its readers, but the replacement cluster starts cold.
briefs.C05: A field guide caches passages with very different fetch costs. Spending a slot on the wrong passage makes some expeditions expensive.
briefs.C06: A conservatory rehearses passages in repeated waves with gaps. Decide what should survive until a section returns.
briefs.C07: A museum guide sees rare valuable references mixed with frequent routine lookups. Preserve the greatest weighted savings under a fixed slot limit.
briefs.C08: A help desk may revisit an old repair passage long after opening it once. Decide how much history should influence the small resident set.
briefs.S01: A copy editor faces a recurring core of verification requests. Choose the next passage to fetch before the pending requests expire.
briefs.S02: An indexer floods a curator with one-off read requests. Schedule limited reading credits so useful near-term requests still finish.
briefs.S03: During a live captioning event, new source lookups arrive in bursts. Choose what to serve under each epoch's limited credits.
briefs.S04: The questions reaching an archive shift from one collection to another mid-session. Adapt the read queue as interest changes.
briefs.S05: A field librarian has requests with widely varying fetch costs. Choose which ones can earn their value before expiry.
briefs.S06: A rehearsal assistant gets waves of repeated read requests separated by quieter periods. Spend credits where timely completion matters.
briefs.S07: A reference desk receives occasional high-value requests among many routine jobs. Schedule time so those gains can actually be realized.
briefs.S08: A case worker returns to earlier passages after long delays. Choose among new and delayed requests under an epoch budget.
